title: Complementary restrictions detect zero fixed-scalar pro-etale sheaves
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $X,Z,U$ schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion and $j:U\to X$ a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion] with complementary ranges. For a fixed-scalar $R$-module sheaf $F$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], if $i^*F$ and $j^*F$ are zero, then $F$ is zero. The coefficient and module universes are $u+1$ when the schemes have universe $u$.

source.place: Pro-etale Cohomology, Tag 09AH; existing source proof isZero_of_isZero_upperStar_of_isCompl via finite jointly surjective quasi-compact detection

proof.text: The two immersions form a finite jointly surjective family of quasi-compact morphisms: closed immersions are quasi-compact, and every point outside the closed range belongs to the open range. Fixed-scalar inverse images along this family jointly detect zero morphisms. Apply this to the identity of F. Its two pullbacks are identities of zero objects, hence zero, so the identity of F is zero. Therefore F is zero. This is the existing source proof via eq_zero_of_forall_upperStar_map_eq_zero, not the arbitrary ring-sheaf localization theorem.
